Global growth is broadening, and business activity is picking up. The Chief Investment Office (CIO) believes 2026 will be shaped by supportive fiscal conditions, rising earnings and an accelerating AI‑industrial investment cycle. “Recently we’ve experienced above-average volatility across the markets,” says Chris Hyzy, Chief Investment Officer for Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank. “This volatility has pressured metals prices and high-growth mega-cap shares as well. In the context of all of this, we’re focusing on six key portfolio considerations we believe matter most this year.”

In his annual roadmap, CEO Neal Mohan positions YouTube as a creator-first studio system, powered by AI and built for the biggest screen in the house. In YouTube’s annual 2026 letter, the company’s CEO, Neal Mohan, lays out a future where the platform is not simply a place to post videos. YouTube is treating the shift like it is already a done deal. Mohan’s framing is direct, marking creators as “the new stars and studios.” Not as a metaphor or as an inspirational line for the stage, but as the actual thesis behind YouTube’s product roadmap. That stat matters because it reframes YouTube from “a social platform people scroll through” to “the biggest living room screen in the country.” YouTube is not fighting for attention on the margins anymore.
